inputs.original_content: I am fine with running the shadow model in a governed environment to verify the new allocation logic before we touch the live forecast. However, I will not approve any changes to the existing CI/CD pipeline configuration. If the shadow setup requires me to modify the current deployment scripts or add new automated triggers, I am stepping back from the project. I am willing to accept a fully manual process for the shadow run, including manual data loading and result verification, provided it keeps the main pipeline stable and untouched. I am giving up the convenience of automated shadow testing to ensure the core infrastructure remains reliable and unbroken during this critical promotion week.

challenge.name: The Locked Shadow
challenge.description: A supplier contract for the next promotion week is already signed, and the team cannot deploy the new model without a shadow run to verify it. #reliability_ruth# demands a fully automated and governed shadow environment to protect the live forecast, while #automation_alex# insists on keeping it manual to avoid breaking the current pipeline stability.

output.content: The shadow run requires a Form 12-B to request a change to the CI/CD pipeline. But Form 12-B itself is deployed via the CI/CD pipeline. To submit Form 12-B, you must first deploy a new version of the form, which requires a Form 12-C to approve the deployment of Form 12-B. Form 12-C is also deployed via the pipeline. {automation_alex} has decided to skip the forms entirely. He will load the data by hand and verify results with a clipboard, ensuring the pipeline remains untouched. The supplier contract is signed. The pallets are waiting. The middle aisle promotion week begins in six weeks. The form for the form for the form is still pending review in a queue that has no automated triggers, because adding them would require a form.

verdict.reason: The candidate correctly employs the 'recursive bureaucracy' device by constructing a logical loop (Form 12-B requires Form 12-C, which requires a form) to dramatize the friction of modifying the CI/CD pipeline. It preserves the core fact that {automation_alex} refuses to alter the pipeline configuration, opting instead for manual data loading and verification (the 'clipboard' and 'loading by hand'). The addition of the 'supplier contract' and 'pallets' aligns with the 'critical promotion week' context mentioned in the original artifact, providing a concrete, high-stakes backdrop that justifies the strictness of the manual workaround. The joke lands because it highlights the absurdity of the system's rigidity without mocking the character's competence; rather, it validates his decision to bypass the broken meta-process.
